f.title: Inform the Director of Pharmaceutical Services immediately of any adverse reaction to a registered product
f.statement: Product Registration Holders, or any person who possesses a registered product, must inform the Director of Pharmaceutical Services immediately of any adverse reaction arising from the use of the registered product (Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Regulation 28, cited as the legal basis of the addendum).
f.legal_basis: Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Reg. 28
f.applicability: Malaysia; NPRA addendum 'Management of Pharmacovigilance Activities within the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA)' to the Malaysian GVP Guidelines for Product Registration Holders (1st edition August 2021), updated October 2025. The addendum mainly describes NPRA's own tasks; only the duties and authority powers that bind Product Registration Holders (PRHs) are curated.
f.processes: Submission operations; Case processing & follow-up; Local PV interfaces

f.title: Comply with the directives and guidelines issued by the Director of Pharmaceutical Services, including on product safety (offence if contravened)
f.statement: The Director of Pharmaceutical Services may issue written directives or guidelines, in particular on product quality, safety and efficacy, labelling and change of particulars; any person who contravenes such directives or guidelines commits an offence. PRHs must therefore comply with the Malaysian GVP guidelines and NPRA safety directives issued under Regulation 29.
f.legal_basis: Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Reg. 29
f.applicability: Malaysia; NPRA addendum 'Management of Pharmacovigilance Activities within the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA)' to the Malaysian GVP Guidelines for Product Registration Holders (1st edition August 2021), updated October 2025. The addendum mainly describes NPRA's own tasks; only the duties and authority powers that bind Product Registration Holders (PRHs) are curated.
f.processes: Regulatory intelligence; Quality system & CAPA; Local PV interfaces

f.title: Submit the product safety document when NPRA requires it because a safety concern has arisen
f.statement: NPRA ensures that the Product Registration Holder submits the product safety document when any concern arises in relation to the product's safety. When such a concern arises, or NPRA requests it, the PRH must submit the product safety document (e.g. periodic safety document) for NPRA assessment.
f.clause: 7. Management of registered medicinal product safety document, 7.2 b)
f.legal_basis: Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Reg. 29
f.applicability: Malaysia; NPRA addendum 'Management of Pharmacovigilance Activities within the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA)' to the Malaysian GVP Guidelines for Product Registration Holders (1st edition August 2021), updated October 2025. The addendum mainly describes NPRA's own tasks; only the duties and authority powers that bind Product Registration Holders (PRHs) are curated.

f.title: Take the actions NPRA directs after assessing the product safety document
f.statement: After assessing the product safety document for new risks, changed risks or changes to the risk-benefit balance, NPRA directs the Product Registration Holder on the necessary action. When so directed, the PRH must take that action.
f.clause: 7. Management of registered medicinal product safety document, 7.2 c)
f.legal_basis: Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Reg. 29
f.applicability: Malaysia; NPRA addendum 'Management of Pharmacovigilance Activities within the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA)' to the Malaysian GVP Guidelines for Product Registration Holders (1st edition August 2021), updated October 2025. The addendum mainly describes NPRA's own tasks; only the duties and authority powers that bind Product Registration Holders (PRHs) are curated.
f.processes: Benefit–risk review; Submission operations; Safety labeling

f.title: Implement the risk minimisation measures NPRA directs; NPRA may act if the PRH fails to comply
f.statement: When risks are identified, NPRA provides direction to Product Registration Holders on implementing risk minimisation measures (such as safety warnings and product information updates). When so directed, the PRH must implement them. NPRA takes regulatory action where the benefit-risk balance is unfavourable or the PRH fails to comply with the required regulatory obligations (e.g. suspension, revocation or cancellation of registration).
f.clause: 9. Risk Assessment and Risk Minimisation Management, 9.1 b)-c)
f.legal_basis: Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Reg. 29

f.title: Be ready for NPRA GVP inspections of the PRH and of parties it engages for PV activities
f.statement: NPRA conducts Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) inspections to ensure that Product Registration Holders, or parties engaged by them to perform pharmacovigilance activities, comply with the Malaysian GVP Guidelines for PRHs and the post-registration safety requirements imposed by NPRA. PRHs must comply with these requirements and be ready, together with their PV service providers, for such inspections.
f.legal_basis: Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Reg. 29
f.applicability: Malaysia; NPRA addendum 'Management of Pharmacovigilance Activities within the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA)' to the Malaysian GVP Guidelines for Product Registration Holders (1st edition August 2021), updated October 2025. The addendum mainly describes NPRA's own tasks; only the duties and authority powers that bind Product Registration Holders (PRHs) are curated.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Partner & vendor oversight; Quality system & CAPA
